items.title: No local estimate of catheter failure before and after the change
items.whyItMatters: The executive is deciding on anecdotes and on one versus two infections, which chance alone can produce.
items.opportunity: Estimate failure for every catheter inserted in the 12 months on each side of 1 March 2025.

items.title: Secular trends and other ward changes
items.whyItMatters: Two consecutive years differ in staffing, patient mix and equipment, not only in policy; a catheter brand change showed up in one retrieved time series (claim c3).
items.opportunity: Plot monthly failure with 12 points on each side, annotate co-interventions, and fit a segmented model.

items.title: Several catheters per patient
items.whyItMatters: Treating catheters as independent inflated a dwell effect in the retrieved methods study (claim c4).
items.opportunity: Model failure with a patient-level frailty term and report catheters per patient.

items.title: Gaps in site assessment and removal reasons
items.whyItMatters: The policy relies on assessment every shift, documented in 83 percent of shifts elsewhere (claim c2), and removal reasons were missing for 11 percent of removals in a validation study (claim c6).
items.opportunity: Report documentation completeness by shift and measure missing removal reasons by period at extraction.

items.title: Harm may be recognised late in some patients
items.whyItMatters: Infiltration was found later in patients with delirium in one retrieved study, visual phlebitis scoring is less reliable on darker skin, and patients with limited English may not report pain.
items.opportunity: Report failure by age group and by interpreter need, and state the limits of visual scoring.

errorsFound: The two bloodstream infections since the change cannot show an effect of the policy; with infection at about 0.08 per 1,000 catheter-days, one or two events a year are expected by chance.
reevaluation: The gaps confirm a cohort of all catheters on both sides of the change, with patient-level clustering, a monthly time series for secular trends, checked removal reasons, and infections reported as counts.
summary: Five gaps; the missing local estimate and secular trends are high severity.
